correctness.rationale: Any bracket-preserving map induces A on the quotient V, a central functional f, and a scalar c on the characteristic derived line. The form condition is b(Ax,Ay)=c b(x,y), and idempotence gives A²=A, c²=c, fA+cf=f. Nondegeneracy makes the c=1 case the identity; c=0 gives exactly an isotropic-image projection with f=theta A. Each U of dimension r has q^r possible graphs and each graph has q^{r(d−r)} projection kernels (complements to U). Counting independent isotropic vectors after each quotient U_j^perp/U_j gives q^j Z_{d−2j} choices, and division by ordered bases gives I_r. Adjoining a hyperbolic plane gives N_0(H⊥W)=q N_0(W)+(q−1)q^{dim W}, verifying the Z formula including the anisotropic base cases. For rank one, P(x)=b(a,x)u with b(a,u)=1. The Gram matrix of (u,a) has determinant −1, so Witt extension proves transitivity for fixed t=b(a,a); representative rescaling changes t by a square and a similitude of multiplier c changes it by c^−1. Comparing b and c b using finite-field isometry by dimension and determinant shows all multipliers occur in even dimension and only square ones in odd dimension. In a hyperbolic splitting with partner v, a=v+beta u+w has t=2 beta+b(w,w), giving q^{d−2} choices for each t. Central shears are transitive on the q graph functionals above a rank-one projection. This proves the two/three orbits and their sizes over every odd prime power. The d=2 cases and the q=3,d=4 examples check: I_1=16,10 respectively, I_2=8 in split dimension four, giving 7130 and 812 total maps. The supplied check was inspected statically, not executed.
residual_risks: Prime-field script coverage alone would not prove arbitrary odd prime powers. There is no assertion on higher-rank conjugacy orbits.

value.rationale: Rank sizes alone conceal inequivalent retractions of the same algebra. The theorem gives the intrinsic obstruction and exact orbit sizes in the first nontrivial rank, showing how the multiplier group changes the answer with dimension parity, and ties this to explicit Witt-sensitive endomorphism-monoid statistics. These data are useful for distinguishing and enumerating idempotents up to algebra automorphism, beyond the classical isotropic-subspace totals.
residual_risks: The value decision concerns rank-one symmetry and Witt-sensitive spectra, not a higher-rank orbit theory.
